title: The Element on Your Ceiling: The Actinoids
subject: Chemistry
objective: An ionisation smoke detector holds about 1 microcurie of americium-241, a man-made actinoid. The actinoids are the fourteen elements thorium (90) to lawrencium (103), filling 5f: [Rn] 5f¹⁻¹⁴ 6d⁰⁻¹ 7s². Because 5f, 6d and 7s are close in energy they show a wide range of oxidation states: +3 is common, but Th reaches +4, Pa +5, U +6 (as in uranyl UO₂²⁺) and Np and Pu +7, after which the maximum falls. 5f electrons shield poorly, so the actinoid contraction is larger than the lanthanoid contraction. The metals are very reactive (boiling water gives oxide and hydride; HCl attacks them; nitric acid forms a protective oxide layer; alkalies have no action). All actinoids are radioactive: Th-232 (≈ 14 billion years) and U-238 (≈ 4.5 billion years) occur in nature, while the elements beyond uranium are man-made and the last ones survive only minutes to hours.

tf.q: Lanthanoids show a wider range of oxidation states than actinoids.
tf.explain: Actinoids show the wider range (up to +7).

tf.q: The actinoid contraction is greater than the lanthanoid contraction.
Only the later actinoids are radioactive.
Thorium and uranium occur in nature in substantial amounts.
Nitric acid dissolves actinoid metals rapidly.
tf.explain: A protective oxide layer forms; HCl attacks them.

ar.a: Assertion: Actinoids show a greater range of oxidation states than lanthanoids. Reason: 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals have comparable energies.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.
ar.explain: Comparable energies allow more electrons to be used.

ar.a: Assertion: Elements beyond uranium are made in reactors and accelerators. Reason: They are too short-lived to survive in nature in significant amounts.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.

short.q: Why do actinoids show a wide range of oxidation states?
short.solution: Their 5f, 6d and 7s levels are close in energy, so different numbers of electrons can be removed or shared; early members reach +4 to +7.

short.q: What is the actinoid contraction and why is it larger than the lanthanoid contraction?
short.solution: The steady decrease in the size of atoms and M³⁺ ions from Th to Lr; it is larger element to element because 5f electrons shield the nuclear charge poorly.

short.q: How does an ionisation smoke detector use americium-241?
short.solution: Am-241 emits alpha particles that ionise the air between two plates, giving a small current; smoke particles reduce the current and the alarm sounds.
